name: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN)
shortDescription: Direct income support of ₹6,000 per year in three equal installments of ₹2,000 every 4 months to all eligible landholding farmer families across India.
fullDescription: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) is a flagship Central Sector scheme with 100% funding from the Government of India. The scheme aims to augment the income of all landholding farmers families across the country to procure agricultural inputs (seeds, fertilizers, equipment) as well as fulfill domestic consumption needs. Under the scheme, financial assistance of ₹6,000 per year is transferred directly into Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) based on land records authenticated by State/UT governments.
ministry: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
department: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
benefitDetails: Financial benefit of ₹6,000 per year payable in three equal four-monthly installments of ₹2,000 each (Period 1: April to July; Period 2: August to November; Period 3: December to March) directly credited via PFMS Aadhaar-based DBT.
eligibilitySummary: All landholding farmer families who own cultivable land registered in their name. Excluded: institutional landholders, farmer families where one or more members hold or held constitutional posts, current/former Ministers, MPs, MLAs, MLCs, Mayors, Chairpersons of District Panchayats, serving/retired officers and employees of Central/State Government ministries and PSUs (except Group D/Multi-Tasking Staff), all retired pensioners whose monthly pension is ₹10,000 or more (excluding Group D), persons who paid income tax in last assessment year, and registered professionals (doctors, engineers, lawyers, CAs, architects).

name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)
shortDescription: Comprehensive crop insurance against yield losses from natural calamities, pests, and post-harvest damages at ultra-low premium rates (1.5% to 2%).
fullDescription: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) provides comprehensive crop insurance coverage and financial stabilization to Indian farmers. The scheme covers prevented sowing, mid-season adversity, standing crop yield losses due to non-preventable natural risks (drought, dry spells, flood, inundation, widespread pest attacks, landslides, natural fire, lightning, storm), and post-harvest losses up to 14 days after harvesting. The farmer pays a maximum premium of only 2% for Kharif food/oilseeds, 1.5% for Rabi food/oilseeds, and 5% for commercial/horticultural crops, with the remaining premium heavily subsidized equally by Central and State Governments.
ministry: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
department: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
benefitDetails: Direct claim settlement credited to the farmer bank account based on Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) and satellite remote sensing. Covers up to 100% sum insured for yield losses, localized calamities (hailstorm, landslide, cloudburst), prevented sowing (25% sum insured), and post-harvest cyclone damage.
eligibilitySummary: All farmers growing notified crops in notified areas defined by the State Government, including sharecroppers and tenant farmers. Enrollment is voluntary for both loanee (KCC holders) and non-loanee farmers.

name: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maandhan Yojana (PM-KMY)
shortDescription: Contributory old-age pension scheme assuring ₹3,000 per month pension to small and marginal farmers on attaining 60 years of age.
fullDescription: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maandhan Yojana (PM-KMY) is an old-age social security pension scheme for Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs) between 18 and 40 years of age. Under this scheme, the farmer makes a modest monthly contribution ranging from ₹55 to ₹200 (based on entry age), and the Central Government contributes an equal 50% matching amount. Upon attaining the age of 60 years, the subscriber receives a guaranteed life-long monthly pension of ₹3,000. Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) acts as the pension fund manager.

name: Soil Health Card Scheme
shortDescription: Field-specific soil health report providing crop-wise customized nutrient and fertilizer recommendations to maximize yield and lower input costs.
fullDescription: The Soil Health Card Scheme is a national flagship initiative to promote balanced crop nutrition and sustainable soil management. Under this scheme, geo-tagged soil samples are collected across agricultural parcels and scientifically analyzed for 12 essential chemical and physical parameters: Primary macronutrients (Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium), Secondary nutrient (Sulphur), Micronutrients (Zinc, Iron, Copper, Manganese, Boron), and Physical parameters (pH, Electrical Conductivity, Organic Carbon). Farmers receive custom recommendations for biofertilizers, compost, and chemical fertilizers for their target crops.
ministry: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
department: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
benefitDetails: 100% free comprehensive soil test report card issued every 2 to 3 years. Provides precise dosage calculations for nitrogen, phosphorus, potash, and micronutrients, reducing excessive fertilizer usage by 15-20% and increasing crop yields by 8-15%.
eligibilitySummary: All farmers cultivating agricultural land in India across all states and union territories. Both landowning farmers and registered cultivators/tenants are eligible.

name: Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY)
shortDescription: Comprehensive health cover of ₹5,00,000 per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization across 28,000+ empanelled hospitals.
fullDescription: Ayushman Bharat - PM-JAY is the world’s largest government-funded health assurance scheme. It provides an annual health cover of ₹5,00,000 per family for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization across more than 28,000 empanelled public and private hospitals nationwide. Beneficiaries are identified from the bottom 40% vulnerable and poor population based on SECC 2011 and state NFSA ration card databases. In 2024-2026, the scheme was universally extended to cover all Indian senior citizens aged 70 and above, regardless of income, with a distinct ₹5,00,000 Ayushman Vay Vandana card. Cashless and paperless from admission to discharge.
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
benefitDetails: Cashless inpatient treatment cover up to ₹5,00,000 per family per annum. Covers 1,949 medical and surgical packages including oncology, neurosurgery, cardiac care, ICU stays, implants, diagnostic tests, medicines, and pre/post hospitalization expenses (3 days pre-hospitalization and 15 days post-hospitalization).
eligibilitySummary: Families categorized as poor and deprived in rural areas (deprivation criteria D1 through D7, excluding specific assets) and specified occupational categories in urban areas based on SECC 2011 or NFSA Ration Card. All senior citizens aged 70 years and above are universally eligible under Ayushman Vay Vandana without income ceiling.

The mission aims to establish robust public health systems capable of responding effectively to public health emergencies. It supports the operationalization of Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (Health & Wellness Centres), Integrated Public Health Laboratories in all 730+ districts, Critical Care Hospital Blocks in districts with over 5 lakh population, and Block Public Health Units across the country.

fullDescription: PM Street Vendor’s AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) is a flagship Central Sector Scheme administered by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA). It facilitates affordable collateral-free working capital loans to urban street vendors, hawkers, thelawalas, and rehris. Features a graded credit ladder: 1st tranche loan of up to ₹10,000 (1-year tenure); on timely repayment, 2nd tranche up to ₹20,000; and 3rd tranche up to ₹50,000. Beneficiaries receive a 7% per annum interest subsidy directly credited into bank accounts, and up to ₹1,200 cashback per year on digital UPI sales.
ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
benefitDetails: Collateral-free working capital loan: ₹10,000 (1st Tranche), ₹20,000 (2nd Tranche), and ₹50,000 (3rd Tranche). 7% interest subsidy credited quarterly to bank account; digital cashback of up to ₹100 per month (₹1,200/year) on UPI merchant transactions.
eligibilitySummary: All street vendors engaged in vending in urban areas on or before the qualifying cut-off date, possessing Certificate of Vending (CoV) / Identity Card issued by Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), or identified in Town Vending Committee (TVC) surveys, or possessing Letter of Recommendation (LoR) from ULB.

name: PM Vishwakarma Scheme (Support for Traditional Artisans and Craftspeople)
shortDescription: Holistic support offering PM Vishwakarma ID, 5-7 days skill training with ₹500/day stipend, ₹15,000 toolkit e-voucher, and collateral-free loans up to ₹3,00,000 at 5% interest.
fullDescription: PM Vishwakarma is a Central Sector Scheme launched with a financial outlay of ₹13,000 crore to provide end-to-end holistic support to traditional artisans and craftspeople working with hands and tools across 18 designated family trades (Carpenter, Boat Maker, Armourer, Blacksmith, Hammer & Toolkit Maker, Locksmith, Sculptor, Goldsmith, Potter, Cobbler, Mason, Basket/Mat/Broom Maker, Doll & Toy Maker, Barber, Garland Maker, Washerman, Tailor, Fishing Net Maker). Features formal government certification, basic and advanced skill training with stipend, ₹15,000 toolkit voucher, collateral-free enterprise credit at 5% concessional interest, and national marketing support.
ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME)
department: Department of MSME & Ministry of Skill Development
benefitDetails: Recognition as Vishwakarma with Certificate and ID Card; Basic Skill Training (5-7 days) with ₹500 per day stipend; ₹15,000 e-voucher for modern toolkits; Collateral-free Enterprise Development Loan: 1st Tranche of ₹1,00,000 (18 months tenure) and 2nd Tranche of ₹2,00,000 (30 months tenure) at concessional interest rate of 5% (with 8% interest subvention by Government).
eligibilitySummary: Artisan or craftsperson working with hands and tools in one of the 18 designated family-based traditional trades. Minimum age 18 years. Must not have availed loans under similar credit schemes (PMEGP, PM MUDRA, PM SVANidhi) in the last 5 years. Limited to one member per family (husband, wife, and unmarried children). Government servants and their family members are not eligible.

name: Atal Pension Yojana (APY)
shortDescription: Guaranteed monthly pension of ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 after age 60 for unorganized sector workers based on low monthly contributions starting from ₹42/month.
fullDescription: Atal Pension Yojana (APY) is a government-backed periodic pension scheme targeted at workers in the unorganized sector. Administered by PFRDA under the National Pension System (NPS) architecture, APY guarantees a lifelong minimum monthly pension of ₹1,000, ₹2,000, ₹3,000, ₹4,000, or ₹5,000 from the age of 60 years. The monthly contribution varies based on the entry age (between 18 and 40 years) and the chosen pension slab. The central government guarantees the pension benefit, meeting any shortfall through fiscal support.
ministry: Ministry of Finance
department: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)
benefitDetails: Guaranteed monthly pension of ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 per month starting at age 60 until death. Upon subscriber death, the same pension is paid to spouse for life; upon death of both subscriber and spouse, the total accumulated pension wealth (corpus up to ₹8.5 Lakhs) is returned to the nominee.
eligibilitySummary: Any Indian citizen aged between 18 and 40 years holding a savings bank or post office account. As per revised rules effective October 1, 2022, any citizen who is or has been an income tax payer is NOT eligible to join APY.

name: Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS - NSAP)
shortDescription: Non-contributory monthly social pension for destitute and Below Poverty Line (BPL) senior citizens aged 60 years and above.
fullDescription: Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS) is a major component of the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development. It provides non-contributory social security monthly pensions to elderly citizens living Below Poverty Line (BPL). The Central Government provides monthly assistance which state governments supplement, ensuring total monthly pension disbursements ranging from ₹1,00,0 to ₹3,000 per month depending on state top-up policies.
ministry: Ministry of Rural Development
benefitDetails: Monthly cash pension transferred via DBT. Central base assistance of ₹200/month for age 60-79 years (enhanced by state governments to ₹1,000-₹2,500/month); Central assistance of ₹500/month for age 80 years and above (enhanced by states up to ₹3,000/month).
eligibilitySummary: Individuals aged 60 years or above belonging to a household categorized as Below Poverty Line (BPL) according to the criteria prescribed by the Government of India or state BPL rosters.

name: Pradhan Mantri Dakshta Aur Kushalta Sampann Hitgrahi (PM-DAKSH)
shortDescription: Free skill development training with stipend (₹1,500 to ₹3,000) and wage compensation for SC, OBC, EBC, DNT youth and sanitation workers.
fullDescription: PM-DAKSH Yojana is implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment through three apex corporations (NSFDC, NBCFDC, and NSKFDC). The scheme provides high-quality market-relevant skill development training to youth belonging to SC, OBC, Economically Backward Classes (EBC), De-Notified Tribes (DNT), and Safai Karamcharis (including waste pickers). Training includes Up-skilling/Re-skilling, Short Term Training, Entrepreneurship Development Programmes (EDP), and Long Term Training, provided completely free of cost with training stipends.

benefitDetails: 100% free skill training; Stipend of ₹1,000 to ₹1,500 per month (for courses >1 month with 80%+ attendance); Wage compensation of ₹2,500 per candidate for up-skilling programs; Free assessment, industry certification, and job placement assistance.

name: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY)
shortDescription: Collateral-free micro-business loans up to ₹20,00,000 under Shishu, Kishore, Tarun, and Tarun Plus categories for non-corporate small enterprises.
fullDescription: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) is a flagship credit initiative launched to "fund the unfunded" by bringing small micro-enterprises and entrepreneurs into the formal financial ecosystem. Loans require no collateral security and are categorized into four tiers: Shishu (loans up to ₹50,000), Kishore (loans from ₹50,001 to ₹5,00,000), Tarun (loans from ₹5,00,001 to ₹10,00,000), and the enhanced Tarun Plus category (up to ₹20,00,000 for entrepreneurs who have previously repaid Tarun loans). Available across all commercial banks, RRBs, Small Finance Banks, and MFIs.
ministry: Ministry of Finance
benefitDetails: Institutional collateral-free financing: Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishore (₹50,001 to ₹5 Lakh), Tarun (₹5 Lakh to ₹10 Lakh), Tarun Plus (up to ₹20 Lakh). No processing fee for Shishu and Kishore; competitive bank interest rates; issuance of MUDRA RuPay Debit Card for hassle-free working capital withdrawals.
eligibilitySummary: Any Indian citizen with a viable business plan for a non-farm income-generating micro-enterprise in manufacturing, trading, or service sector, as well as allied agricultural activities (dairy, poultry, fisheries, agro-processing).

name: Stand-Up India Scheme for SC/ST and Women Entrepreneurs
shortDescription: Bank loans between ₹10,00,000 and ₹1,00,00,000 for setting up greenfield enterprises in manufacturing, services, or trading by SC/ST or woman entrepreneurs.
fullDescription: Stand-Up India Scheme facilitates institutional bank loans between ₹10 Lakhs and ₹1 Crore to at least one Scheduled Caste (SC) or Scheduled Tribe (ST) borrower and at least one woman borrower per bank branch of all scheduled commercial banks. The credit is meant for setting up a greenfield (first-time) enterprise in manufacturing, services, agri-allied activities, or the trading sector. Supported by Credit Guarantee Fund for Stand Up India (CGFSI) managed by NCGTC.
ministry: Ministry of Finance
benefitDetails: Composite loan (term loan + working capital) covering up to 85% of project cost between ₹10 Lakh and ₹1 Crore. Repayable in 7 years with an initial moratorium period up to 18 months. Concessional interest rate and collateral-free credit guarantee coverage.
eligibilitySummary: SC/ST individuals or Women entrepreneurs aged 18 years and above setting up a greenfield enterprise. For non-individual enterprises, at least 51% of shareholding and controlling stake must be held by SC/ST or woman entrepreneur. Borrower should not be in default to any bank or financial institution.

name: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY)
shortDescription: High-interest (8.2% p.a.), triple tax-exempt (EEE) government savings scheme for girl children opened before age 10 for higher education and marriage.
fullDescription: Sukanya Samriddhi Account is a sovereign-backed small savings scheme launched under the "Beti Bachao Beti Padhao" campaign to build a secure financial corpus for girl children. It currently offers one of the highest interest rates among Indian small savings instruments (8.2% per annum, compounded annually). Enjoys complete triple tax exemption (EEE status: investment deduction under Section 80C, tax-free annual interest, and tax-free maturity amount). Accounts can be opened in any post office or authorized commercial bank branch.
ministry: Ministry of Finance / Women and Child Development
benefitDetails: 8.2% annual compounded interest. Minimum deposit ₹250, maximum deposit ₹1,50,000 per financial year. Triple tax exemption under IT Act (EEE). Partial withdrawal up to 50% allowed for higher education after girl turns 18. Account matures after 21 years from opening date or at marriage after age 18.
eligibilitySummary: Resident Indian girl child aged 10 years or younger at the time of account opening. Natural parents or legal guardians can open the account. name: Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY)
shortDescription: Direct maternity cash benefit of ₹5,000 for first child and ₹6,000 for second child (if girl) for pregnant and lactating mothers.
fullDescription: Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) is a Centrally Sponsored direct benefit transfer conditional cash scheme under the umbrella Mission Shakti. The scheme provides cash incentive as partial wage compensation for pregnant women and lactating mothers (PW&LM), encouraging early ante-natal check-ups (ANC), institutional delivery, and child vaccination. Under revamped Mission Shakti rules, mothers receive ₹5,000 in two installments for the first child, and an incentive of ₹6,000 in a single installment for the second child provided the newborn child is a girl.
ministry: Ministry of Women and Child Development
benefitDetails: First Child: ₹5,000 total (Installment 1: ₹3,000 on registration of pregnancy and at least one ANC within 6 months; Installment 2: ₹2,000 on registration of child birth and completion of first cycle of immunizations). Second Child: ₹6,000 in a single installment if the second child is female, upon birth registration and full primary immunization.
eligibilitySummary: Pregnant women and lactating mothers who belong to socially and economically disadvantaged categories (holding BPL/NFSA ration card, e-Shram card, MGNREGA job card, PM-JAY card, SC/ST, or family income < ₹8L). Excludes mothers in regular employment with Central or State Government or Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs).

fullDescription: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) is a flagship joint initiative coordinated by the Ministry of Women and Child Development, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and Ministry of Education. Operating nationwide across all 765+ districts, BBBP addresses the declining Child Sex Ratio (CSR) and works to eliminate gender-biased sex selection (enforcing PC-PNDT Act), promote institutional deliveries, ensure 100% girl child secondary education retention, provide career counseling in STEM, and eradicate child marriage.

It operates through four distinct verticals: Beneficiary-Led Construction (BLC), Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP), Affordable Rental Housing Complexes (ARHC), and the Interest Subsidy Scheme (ISS) for home loans up to ₹25 Lakhs (property value up to ₹35 Lakhs) for EWS, LIG, and Middle Income Group (MIG) families.

benefitDetails: Financial subsidy of ₹2.50 Lakhs (under BLC and AHP verticals paid in milestone-based installments). Under Interest Subsidy Scheme (ISS), 4% interest subsidy on home loans up to ₹25 Lakhs (maximum total subsidy benefit of ₹1.80 Lakhs) credited upfront into the home loan account, significantly reducing EMIs.

shortDescription: Financial assistance of ₹1,20,000 (plains) or ₹1,30,000 (hills) plus 90-95 days MGNREGA wages and ₹12,000 toilet aid for constructing a 25 sq.m pucca house.
fullDescription: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Gramin (PMAY-G) is a premier rural housing scheme implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development. It aims to achieve "Housing for All" in rural areas by providing direct financial assistance to all houseless families and those living in dilapidated/kutcha houses. Beneficiaries build a minimum 25 sq. meter pucca house with a hygienic cooking space. Eligible households are identified strictly from SECC 2011 and updated Awaas+ survey lists verified by local Gram Sabhas.
ministry: Ministry of Rural Development
benefitDetails: Direct unit financial assistance of ₹1,20,000 in plain areas and ₹1,30,000 in hilly/difficult/NE states and IAP districts. Additionally, 90 to 95 person-days of unskilled labor support under MGNREGA (approx ₹20,000 to ₹25,000), ₹12,000 financial aid for toilet construction under Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen), and free LPG connection under PM Ujjwala Yojana.

name: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)
shortDescription: Legal guarantee of 100 days of wage employment per financial year to rural households whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work.
fullDescription: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) is an Indian social welfare legal enactment that guarantees the "right to work". It legally mandates the provision of at least 100 days of guaranteed wage employment in every financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work. If employment is not provided within 15 days of applying, the applicant is entitled to a statutory unemployment allowance. Wages are notified by the Ministry of Rural Development and disbursed directly via Aadhaar Based Payment System (ABPS).

benefitDetails: Statutory guarantee of 100 days of wage employment per rural household per year (extended up to 150 days in natural calamity notified areas). Wages disbursed directly into bank accounts via ABPS within 15 days of work muster roll closure. Statutory state-notified daily wages range from ₹234 to ₹374 per day.

fullDescription: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) is a flagship poverty alleviation programme implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development. It mobilizes rural poor women into Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and federations, building financial autonomy and sustainable livelihood micro-enterprises. Under the national "Lakhpati Didi" initiative, DAY-NRLM provides technical training, market linkages, and credit access to enable SHG women to earn a sustainable annual income of at least ₹1,00,000. benefitDetails: Revolving Fund (RF) of ₹20,000 to ₹30,000 per SHG; Community Investment Fund (CIF) up to ₹1,50,000; Collateral-free bank loans up to ₹10 Lakhs (and up to ₹20 Lakhs under SHG Bank Linkage); Interest subvention reducing effective interest rate to 7% (and 4% for prompt repayment on loans up to ₹3 Lakhs); Specialized training in drone piloting (Drone Didi), agro-enterprises, and dairy value chains.
